back: The removal of soil, especially topsoil, by water and wind faster than new soil forms.
Even removal of a thin layer of topsoil over a wide area; signs: pale patches, exposed roots, stone pedestals.
Rills are small channels removable by cultivation; gullies are deep channels that implements cannot cross.
Suspension (dust), saltation (bouncing grains), surface creep (rolling grains).
Overgrazing, deforestation, cultivating slopes and stream banks, veld fires, poor tillage.
Agents (water, wind) move soil; causes (overgrazing, burning) make soil vulnerable.
Siltation of dams and rivers, flooding, water pollution, damaged roads and bridges, dust.

front: Soil loss per hectare from a plot
back: Soil lost (kg) ÷ plot area (ha); plot area in ha = m² ÷ 10,000.
